{{Short description|German amateur astronomer (born 1964)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}

|}

'''Erwin Schwab''' (born 1964) is a German amateur [[astronomer]] and [[discoverer of minor planets]], who works at the [[GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research]], near [[Darmstadt]], Germany.<ref name="MPC-object-Erwinschwab" /><ref name=FR>[http://www.fr-online.de/rhein-main/darmstadt/planet-darmstadt/-/1472858/4531360/-/index.html "Neuer Asteroid entdeckt: Planet Darmstadt" (New asteroid discovered: Planet Darmstadt)], ''[[Frankfurter Rundschau]]'' 4 August 2010 {{in lang|de}}</ref><ref name=fair>{{Cite web |url=http://www-win.gsi.de/FAIR-Newsletter/Download_Center/NL_No15.pdf |title=FAIR Newsletter No.15, April 2010, Page 10 |access-date=13 August 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110719034923/http://www-win.gsi.de/FAIR-Newsletter/Download_Center/NL_No15.pdf |archive-date=19 July 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He has discovered and co-discovered more than 80 [[asteroid]]s<ref name="MPC-Discoverers" /> from the [[Starkenburg Observatory|Starkenburg]] {{Obscode|611}}, Tzec Maun {{Obscode|D25}} and Taunus observatories {{Obscode|B01}}. As volunteer scientist for the [[European Space Agency]] (ESA) he recovered [[near-Earth object]]s and [[comet]]s.<ref>[https://neo.ssa.esa.int/-/lost-asteroid-rediscovered-with-a-little-help-from-esa Lost asteroid rediscovered with a little help from ESA], ESA, 12 October 2012. Retrieved 16 February 2022.</ref><ref>[https://www.caha.es/news/releases-mainmenu-163/12812-recovering-of-comet-catalina-with-the-schmidt-telescope Recovering of comet Catalina with the Schmidt telescope] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230716125314/https://www.caha.es/news/releases-mainmenu-163/12812-recovering-of-comet-catalina-with-the-schmidt-telescope |date=16 July 2023 }}, Centro Astronómico Hispano-Alemán, April 2018. Retrieved 16 February 2022.</ref><ref name=2018-H30>[https://minorplanetcenter.net/mpec/K18/K18H30.html Minor Planet Electronic Circulars 2018-H30]</ref> From 2014 to 2021 he recovered 30 lost comets, which equates to about 25% of the worldwide proportion in that timespan.<ref>[http://erwinschwab.de/comet recoveries of comets in cooperation with the European Space Agency (ESA)], private homepage Erwin Schwab. Retrieved 16 February 2022.</ref><ref>[http://erwinschwab.de/CometRecoveriesStatistics.htm comet recoveries statistic], private homepage Erwin Schwab. Retrieved 16 February 2022.</ref> Using the Schmidt telescope at [[Calar Alto Observatory]] {{Obscode|Z84}} to search for a lost comet he discovered in 2019 a unique [[variable star]] – the first known eclipsing stream-fed [[intermediate polar]], cataloged as J1832.4-1627 (VSX-Id of [[American Association of Variable Star Observers|AAVSO]]: 000-BNG-512)<ref>[https://www.caha.es/news/releases-mainmenu-163/14157-the-first-binary-star-of-its-kind-discovered-with-the-schmidt-telescope The first binary star of its kind discovered with the Schmidt telescope] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230716125311/https://www.caha.es/news/releases-mainmenu-163/14157-the-first-binary-star-of-its-kind-discovered-with-the-schmidt-telescope |date=16 July 2023 }}, Centro Astronómico Hispano-Alemán, 23 November 2021. Retrieved 16 February 2022.</ref><ref>[https://phys.org/news/2021-11-j18324-eclipsing-stream-fed-intermediate-polar.html J1832.4-1627 is the first eclipsing stream-fed intermediate polar, study finds], phys.org, 15 November 2021. Retrieved 16 February 2022.</ref><ref>[https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.02752 J1832.4-1627, the first eclipsing stream-fed intermediate polar], Beuermann, K., Breitenstein, P. & Schwab, E. 2022, A&A, 657, A101</ref><ref>[https://www.aavso.org/vsx/index.php?view=detail.top&oid=844744 The International Variable Star Index], Discovery credit entry. Retrieved 16 February 2022.</ref>

== Biography ==

Schwab was born in [[Heppenheim]],<ref name=FR/><ref name=Darmstadt>Sabine Schiner, [http://www.echo-online.de/suedhessen/darmstadt/-Darmstadt-schwebt-zwischen-Mars-und-Jupiter;art1231,1053721 "'Darmstadt' schwebt zwischen Mars und Jupiter" ("Darmstadt" orbits between Mars and Jupiter)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100806153400/http://www.echo-online.de/suedhessen/darmstadt/-Darmstadt-schwebt-zwischen-Mars-und-Jupiter;art1231,1053721 |date=6 August 2010 }}, ''Darmstädter Echo'' 4 August 2010 {{in lang|de}}</ref> where he started observing minor planets at the [[Starkenburg Observatory]] in 1981.<ref name=letter>[http://www.erwinschwab.de/pdf/CBAT_Antwort.pdf Letter from International Astronomical Union]</ref>

== Honors and awards ==

The [[Observatorio Astronómico de La Sagra]] in Spain has named the main-belt asteroid [[185638 Erwinschwab]] in his honour.<ref name="MPC-object-Erwinschwab" /><ref name=erwinschwab>Minor Planet Circular # 66244, published 7 June 2009.</ref><ref>[http://www.minorplanets.org/OLS/names.html#Erwinschwab Names given to LSSS asteroid discoveries: Erwinschwab], Observatorio Astronómico de La Sagra, minorplanets.org, 25 February 2010, retrieved 13 August 2010.</ref>

== Discoveries ==

One which he discovered is named after his parents, Elfriede and Erwin Schwab.<ref>[http://www.starkenburg-sternwarte.de/asteroiden/hps/namen.htm Kleinplaneten-Namen], Starkenburg Observatory, 28 June 2010, retrieved 13 August 2010.</ref> Schwab has discovered asteroids at Starkenburg, Tzec Maun<ref name=tzecmaun>[http://portal.tzecmaun.org/wiki/index.php?title=Asteroid_Astrometry_and_Reporting&redirect=no Asteroid Astrometry and Reporting] {{Webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20130416033317/http://portal.tzecmaun.org/wiki/index.php?title=Asteroid_Astrometry_and_Reporting&redirect=no |date=16 April 2013 }}, Tzec Maun Observatory wiki.</ref> as well as at the Taunus Observatory.<ref name="MPC-Discoverers" /> Some minor planet are named for German cities such as [[204852 Frankfurt]], [[241418 Darmstadt]], and [[243440 Colonia]] (Cologne), while the Jupiter-trojans [[192220 Oicles]] and [[221917 Opites]] are named after figures from Greek mythology.<!--

[[Gesellschaft für Schwerionenforschung#Future evolution|FAIR]].<ref name=FR/><ref name=Darmstadt/><ref>On 17 February 2010, Schwab gave a public lecture at the Centre for Heavy Ion Research on "’FAIR’ zwischen Mars und Jupiter – wie der Kleinplanet Nr. 204873 zu seinem Namen kam" ("FAIR" between Mars and Jupiter – how minor planet 204873 came by its name). [http://www.helmholtz.de/en/news/press_and_news/zentrum/gsi_helmholtz_centre_for_heavy_ion_research/ Press Release of 9 February 2010], GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research, retrieved 13 August 2010.</ref>

--> He also co-discovered {{mp|2009 DM|45}}, an unnumbered Apollo asteroid and [[potentially hazardous object]].<ref name=2009-D81>[http://minorplanetcenter.org/mpec/K09/K09D81.html Minor Planet Electronic Circulars 2009-D81]</ref>
